newsitem.title: TURKEY: New Turk government says it addressing IMF worries. [CORRECTED 00:20 GMT 7/8]
newsitem.headline: New Turk government says it addressing IMF worries. [CORRECTED 00:20 GMT 7/8]

text.p: Turkey's treasury chief said the new economic administration in Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz's six-week-old government is taking measures to stabilise the economy and lower inflation -- key concerns in a recent IMF report.

"The IMF report is correct. However, it is an assessment of the previous era in the economy. The new government began to take measures which will also address the issues stated in the IMF report," Treasury undersecretary Mahfi Egilmez told Reuters.

In a summary of its annual review of the Turkish economy prepared after a consultation visit by a Fund team to Turkey in April, the IMF urged Turkey to embark on a bold and comprehensive programme of stabilisation policies and structural reforms to lower inflation and set the economy on a sustainable growth path.
Egilmez said the new economy management has been taking some steps since early July -- which he says are part of stabilisation measures.

"One of them is the recent public sector price adjustment which will stop erosion of resources. Then we signed a protocol with the central bank (corrects from treasury) and started studies on the concept of a financeable deficit," Egilmez said.
"They are all elements of a stabilisation programme," he added.
The treasury and central bank signed a protocol last week to cooperate in fighting chronic inflation running at around 85 percent on a year-on-year basis.
Under the seven-point accord, the treasury agreed to safeguard the bank's monetary programme.

The treasury's heavy reliance on central bank resources and lack of coordination between the two institutions on domestic borrowing policies has distorted financial stability and prevented the bank from implementing a tight monetary policy in the past.
Egilmez said the treasury had recieved positive feedback from the IMF and World Bank about the steps taken so far.

"The economy was put on a right path. But the IMF did not have the opportunity to assess it," he said. The report was finalised at a July 9 meeting of the IMF board shortly before the new government won a confidence vote in parliament.
Egilmez was appointed treasury chief on July 16.
After taking office, the government revised 1997 economic targets and raised prices of various goods and services. It also pledged to speed up sell-offs, but no concrete step have been taken yet.
